source: Waters & King (1970), Rheologica Acta 9(3) 345-355; closed-form transient Poiseuille for Oldroyd-B

provenance.citation: Waters, ND and King, MJ (1970), 'Unsteady flow of an elastico-viscous liquid', Rheologica Acta 9(3) 345-355, Springer

convergence_evidence: cross-checked against Basilisk poiseuille-oldroydb.ref at three grid levels {16x16, 32x32, 64x64}; analytic curve sits within Basilisk scatter

formula.beta_complex_def: beta_n = sqrt(alpha_n^2 - E * n^2)  (complex if alpha_n^2 < E * n^2)
formula.Y_def: Y in [-1, 1] (h is the half-channel height)
formula.U_def: U = u_x / u_avg_steady where u_avg_steady = -(dp/dx) * h^2 / (3 * mu0)
formula.scope: Suddenly-applied pressure-gradient start-up between two no-slip walls
formula.convention_notes: beta is the SOLVENT viscosity ratio (= mus / mu0); a fluid with no polymer has beta=1 and reduces to Newtonian.

parameters.KF_modes_note: Basilisk uses 8 modes; converged at single-precision tolerance for E ~ 1. For E larger, more modes needed.

tolerance_pass_fail.rationale: Basilisk reports L2 convergence between 16x16 and 64x64 around order 2

notes: Couette start-up shares the same eigenvalue structure (alpha_n, beta_n). The inhomogeneous part differs and is not encoded here; this JSON serves Poiseuille; L2 (Couette) STUB will reference this entry for the eigenstructure and add the Couette-specific inhomogeneous coefficient.
